title: Default Fuhrman Lab Pipeline for Exact Amplicon Sequence Variant Calling
author: Jesse Mcnichol
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.vi9e4h6

steps.title: Verify conda environment
steps.instruction: In a terminal run `which conda` and confirm the output is `/home/anaconda/miniconda2/bin/conda`; if not, follow the Guidelines and Warnings or install conda before proceeding.

steps.title: Create base directory and raw data folder
steps.instruction: Make a new folder with an informative name (the “base directory”). Inside it create a README file and a subfolder named `00-raw`. Place the demultiplexed FASTQ files there, naming them `*.R1.fastq.gz` for forward reads and `*.R2.fastq.gz` for reverse reads. If files are not gzipped, run `gzip *` (or `pigz` for parallel compression). Verify gzip integrity with `head yourfile` (gibberish output means properly gzipped).

steps.title: Clone pipeline repository and set permissions
steps.instruction: Clone the pipeline with `git clone https://github.com/jcmcnch/eASV-pipeline-for-515Y-926R.git`. Enter the cloned directory, make all scripts executable with `chmod a+x ./*` and confirm with `ls -la`. (Optional) Add the script directory to your PATH by appending `export PATH="/path/to/dir:$PATH"` to `~/.bashrc` and reloading with `source ~/.bashrc`.

steps.title: Trim primers with cutadapt
steps.instruction: From the directory that contains the `00-raw` folder, run the script `00-run-cutadapt.sh` (found in `00-trimming-sorting-scripts`). After it finishes, inspect the log file to ensure that primer‑containing reads are identified at ~100 % and that output file sizes are reasonable. If the script fails, check that file naming follows the `*.R1.fastq.gz` / `*.R2.fastq.gz` pattern and that the script is executable.

steps.title: Separate 16S and 18S reads
steps.instruction: From the base directory run `01-sort-16S-18S-bbsplit.sh`. The script splits mixed reads into 16S and 18S folders and copies in‑silico mock files. Verify the log shows a very high sorting proportion (≈100 % for real reads and 100 % for mocks) before proceeding.

steps.title: Enter PROK analysis directory
steps.instruction: Change into the `02-PROKs` directory. All subsequent PROK scripts (prefixed with “P”) are run from here. Optionally create a subfolder `scripts` and copy the `P*` scripts into it so they can be invoked as `./scripts/your-step.sh`.

steps.title: Check PROK fastq file sizes
steps.instruction: List the files in `02-PROKs/00-fastq` and confirm they are of reasonable (non‑zero) size. Occasional zero‑size files are expected for pure EUK mocks, but many zero‑size files indicate a sorting problem.

steps.title: Create PROK manifest
steps.instruction: Run `P00-create-manifest.sh` inside `02-PROKs`. The script removes empty files and writes a CSV manifest. Open the resulting CSV in a spreadsheet program and verify that sample IDs are <32 characters and correctly spelled; the manifest IDs must match those used later for metadata and barplots.

steps.title: Import PROK sequences
steps.instruction: Execute `P01-import.sh` to import the FASTQ files listed in the manifest into a QIIME 2 artifact (a `.qza` file) that records the raw data and software versions.

steps.title: Visualize PROK quality and set trims
steps.instruction: Run `P02-visualize-quality_R1-R2.sh`. Open the generated visualization artifact (e.g., with `qiime tools view`). Choose trimming lengths that keep the median quality score ≥30 and provide at least 20 nt overlap for merging. Record the chosen trim values in your computational notebook for the next step.

steps.title: Export DADA2 results and inspect stats
steps.instruction: Run `P04-export-DADA2-results.sh`. This writes human‑readable files; open `03-DADA2d/stats.tsv` and confirm that the majority of sequences passed through (low loss indicates appropriate trimming).

steps.title: Classify PROK eASVs with SILVA
steps.instruction: Run `P05-classify-eASVs.sh`. The script assigns taxonomy to each eASV using a classifier built from SILVA 132 trimmed to the default primer region (k‑mer based, suitable for both prokaryotes and eukaryotes).

steps.title: Create sample metadata file
steps.instruction: Generate a template with `P06-make-sample-metadata-file.py manifest.csv > sample-metadata.tsv`. Edit the TSV in a text editor to add relevant metadata (e.g., date, size fraction) and save it as tab‑separated plain text.

steps.title: Generate PROK barplot
steps.instruction: Run `P07-make-barplot.sh`. The script combines abundance, taxonomy, and the sample‑metadata file to produce an interactive barplot. Open the plot, verify that dominant taxa are as expected, and look for possible contaminants.

steps.title: Split chloroplast/mitochondria and reclassify
steps.instruction: Run `P09-split-mito-chloro-PhytoRef-reclassify.sh`. This separates chloroplast sequences, re‑classifies them with PhytoRef, and merges the new taxonomy with the SILVA‑based classifications. Note that PhytoRef chloroplast taxonomy begins with `Kingdom:Eukaryota`.

steps.title: Export tables with taxonomy
steps.instruction: Run `P10-generate-tsv-biom-tables-with-taxonomy.sh`. The script exports each `feature-table.qza` it finds as a TSV with taxonomy added, placing results in `10-exports/`. Verify the exported tables look reasonable and that mock communities are present.

steps.title: Convert tables to proportions and filter
steps.instruction: Run `P10-transform-tsv-to-proportions.sh`. The underlying Python script (`transform-ESV-tsv-to-proportions.py`) filters out eASVs with relative abundance <0.01 % and retains the set of eASVs that together account for 99 % of total abundance in each sample. Check the help output with `transform-ESV-tsv-to-proportions.py -h` if needed.

steps.title: Create subsetted barplots
steps.instruction: Run `P12-make-subsetted-barplots.sh`. This produces barplots for various subsets (e.g., without chloroplasts, without mitochondria, chloroplast‑only, mitochondria‑only) using the PhytoRef‑enhanced taxonomy.

steps.title: Exclude selected samples from barplots
steps.instruction: Prepare a plain‑text file `sample-to-keep.tsv` listing sample IDs to retain (e.g., exclude mocks or replicates). Then run `P13-exclude-samples-from-barplots.sh` which uses that list to generate filtered barplots.

steps.title: Optional eASV clustering
steps.instruction: If desired, cluster eASVs with VSEARCH by running `P08-optionally-cluster-eASVs.sh <identity>` (e.g., `P08-optionally-cluster-eASVs.sh 99` for 99 % clustering). The script creates a new output folder for each identity level and writes a `.uc` file. Later, parse cluster membership with `parse_VSEARCH_cluster_membership_from_UC_file.py`.

steps.title: Enter EUK analysis directory
steps.instruction: Change into the `02-EUKs` directory; all EUK scripts (prefixed with “E”) are run from here.

steps.title: Create EUK manifest
steps.instruction: Run `E00-create-manifest-viz.sh` to generate a manifest file for the EUK reads.

steps.title: Import EUK sequences
steps.instruction: Run `E01-import.sh` to import the EUK FASTQ files into a QIIME 2 artifact.

steps.title: Visualize EUK quality and decide trims
steps.instruction: Run `E02-visualize-quality_R1-R2.sh` and open the visualization. Choose trim lengths that keep median quality ≥30 and provide sufficient overlap. Example values: forward = 221 bp, reverse = 192 bp (or shorter reverse such as 120 bp if needed). Record the chosen lengths for the next step.

steps.title: Run DADA2 on EUK reads
steps.instruction: Execute `P03-DADA2.sh <trimleft> <trimright>` (e.g., `P03-DADA2.sh 214 187`). The script requires the two trim lengths and writes them to a file for future reference. It runs the QIIME 2 `dada2 denoise-paired` workflow.

steps.title: QC EUK eASV table against mocks
steps.instruction: Open `03-DADA2d/feature-table.biom.tsv` in a spreadsheet, delete the top header row, and sort by the column corresponding to the in‑silico staggered mock. Compare the real mock column to the in‑silico mock: the number of rows should be equal or lower. Copy the IDs of questionable eASVs to a plain‑text file, extract their sequences with `seqtk subseq dna-sequences.fasta questionable-eASVs.fasta`, then blast them using `16s-mock-blast.sh` (or `18s-mock-blast.sh` for EUK) as `16s-mock-blast.sh questionable-eASVs.fasta output.tsv`. Sort the output by mismatches and flag any with a single mismatch as potentially spurious. Investigate high‑abundance occurrences in other samples for bleed‑through.

steps.title: Cut EUK reads to chosen lengths
steps.instruction: Run `E03-bbduk-cut-reads.sh` to trim the forward and reverse reads to the lengths decided in the visualization step.

steps.title: Fuse trimmed EUK reads
steps.instruction: Run `E04-fuse-EUKs-withoutNs.sh` to concatenate the trimmed forward and reverse reads into a single sequence per fragment (no intervening N). When publishing, note that these are artificially fused sequences.

steps.title: Import concatenated EUK reads
steps.instruction: Run `E05-create-manifest-concat.sh` to build a manifest for the fused reads, then `E06-import-concat.sh` to import them as a QIIME 2 artifact.

steps.title: Visualize fused EUK read quality
steps.instruction: Run `E07-visualize-quality-single-seqs.sh` and open the resulting visualization. Expect a quality drop in the middle (where the original reverse read ended) with higher quality at both ends; deviations indicate a problem.

steps.title: Run DADA2 on fused EUK reads
steps.instruction: Execute `E08-DADA2.sh`. No trimming arguments are needed because all reads are now the same length; the script runs `qiime dada2 denoise-single`.

steps.title: Export fused EUK DADA2 results
steps.instruction: Run `E09-export-DADA2-results.sh`. Check `stats.tsv` for sequence retention (≈80 % is typical). Examine the eASV table as in the PROK QC step, using `18s-mock-blast.sh` to compare against the 18S mock database.

steps.title: Proceed with remaining PROK‑style steps
steps.instruction: Follow the remaining numbered scripts (e.g., further barplot generation, sample exclusion, optional clustering) as described for the PROK pipeline, applying them to the EUK results where appropriate.
